cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Delegate Downward
cards.instruction: Make someone accept an unwanted responsibility by placing them lower in the hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You're my deputy. You'll answer the inspector's complaints.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Most of them concern decisions you made.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Exactly. You handle the details below decision-making level.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The inspector wants whoever signs the replies at tomorrow's hearing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign as deputy, then. You can represent me without giving the impression we're equals.

mechanism: A keeps decision authority personally while assigning complaint details, signatures and public representation to a lower-ranked deputy.
confusable: Simple delegation can be neutral; D53 requires the unwanted responsibility to be accepted because the helper remains below A.
comparison: Inspection replies and hearing attendance differ from the sink scene promotion used to assign late lockup.
seedUse: The existing D53-b explicit below-decision-making boundary and deputy signature sustain the combined hierarchy mechanism.
